overview: Two opposite metabolic pathways controlling how glucose is stored versus released as glycogen.
genZNote: Glycogenesis: stashing sugar for later. Glycogenolysis: breaking into the stash when you need it now.

aspects.label: Direction of the Pathway
aspects.valueA: Converts excess glucose into glycogen for storage.
aspects.valueB: Breaks down stored glycogen back into glucose.

aspects.label: Triggering Hormone
aspects.valueA: Stimulated by insulin, released after a meal when blood glucose is high.
aspects.valueB: Stimulated by glucagon (and adrenaline), released when blood glucose is low.

aspects.label: Main Site
aspects.valueB: Mainly liver cells (muscle glycogen is used locally, not released into blood).

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Only the liver can release glucose from glycogen back into the bloodstream — muscle glycogen stays local and is used only by the muscle itself.
overlay.memoryTrick: Genesis = creation (making glycogen). Lysis = breakdown (breaking glycogen).
overlay.commonMisconception: Glycogenolysis is not the same as gluconeogenesis — glycogenolysis breaks down existing glycogen, while gluconeogenesis builds new glucose from non-carbohydrate sources.
